defects: ANSWERING THE DIRECT QUESTION: YES, task_metadata.py needs correcting. It still reads '== live weightwatcher 0.7.7 across ALL 49 gpt2 modules'; the scan is 48 and I confirmed _meta_n_modules_scanned = 48 with _meta_n_modules_excluded_unembedding = 1 on gpt2. The parity claim remains true of the numbers -- it was always 48 shared rows, since WW's 49th is transformer.wpe, which BLME never scanned -- but the count is wrong and the sentence now sits directly above an ARCHIVE INCOMPATIBILITY note that says the scan is 48, so the entry contradicts itself.

A residual hole in the exclusion, narrower than the one just closed: the name-list fallback fires ONLY when get_output_embeddings() returns None. If an architecture returns a module that is not in TARGET_MODULES (a tied nn.Embedding, say) while a vocabulary-sized nn.Linear head also exists under a nested name, identity matches nothing AND the fallback is suppressed. None of the six architectures I tested does this, so it is latent, not live. Making the fallback additive (`(module is _out_emb) or _leaf in _EXCLUDE_SUFFIXES or name in _EXCLUDE_SUFFIXES`) costs nothing -- I grepped transformers and every model using `output_projection` uses it for the unembedding (biogpt, fsmt, trocr).

Still no x_min, KS distance, tail size or fit status emitted for alpha_official, so the source paper's own warning that fits with alpha >> 6 'may not be very reliable' cannot be checked downstream. All four are computed inside _pl_mle_alpha_ks and discarded. roberta-base's max_alpha is 7.82 and BERT's 8.51, both in that band.

The legacy Hill family (avg/min/max/std/median_alpha) is still 5 of the emitted scalars under the bare name 'alpha' while correlating with alpha_official at Spearman 0.3817 over gpt2's modules. The docstring now says so plainly (and correctly retracts the earlier 'ranking is preserved' claim), but the key names do not.

A degenerate fit still returns the sentinel alpha = 0.0 (when log_sum <= 0 or top_k[-1] <= 1e-6) and that 0.0 is averaged into avg_alpha and can become min_alpha. Unreachable on the real weights I measured -- min_alpha is 3.481 (gpt2), 3.908 (roberta), 3.864 (bert) -- but it is the same class of defect as the clip that was just correctly removed; NaN plus nan-aware aggregation would be right.
avg_stable_rank is emitted raw and is dimension-bounded by min(m,n); still no stable_rank/min(m,n) companion.

Off-by-one in the Hill tail (cosmetic, and it matches WW): x_min = top_k[-1] is itself included in the sum, giving alpha = 1 + k/sum_{i<k} log(x_i/x_k) rather than the textbook 1 + (k-1)/sum -- worth +0.65% at k = 153.

_meta_n_alpha_over_old_cap reads 0 on gpt2, roberta-base and bert-base-uncased, so for these models the clip removal is a no-op; the archive note's claim that it matters is carried by gemma-2b alone and is untested here.
fix: The exclusion fix is correct and should stand -- it is exact on all six architectures I tested and is the only rule that catches roberta's lm_head.decoder and BERT's cls.predictions.decoder. (1) Correct task_metadata.py's 'ALL 49 gpt2 modules' to 48; the entry currently contradicts the archive note two sentences later. (2) Make the name fallback additive rather than conditional on the accessor returning None, closing the latent nested-head-plus-non-Linear-accessor case at zero cost. (3) Emit the x_min, KS distance, n_tail and fit status that _pl_mle_alpha_ks already computes -- roberta and BERT both report max_alpha in the range the source paper calls unreliable. (4) Rename avg/min/max/std/median_alpha to hill_alpha_sv_* so the bare name 'alpha' belongs to the official estimator. (5) Return NaN rather than the 0.0 sentinel for degenerate fits. (6) Add stable_rank/min(m,n) as an explicitly named dimensionless companion. (7) Extend the archive-incompatibility note: it records the gpt2 move (11.100879 -> 10.942422) but not that roberta-base and BERT change too (avg_alpha_hat -0.85% and -1.86%), which is where the old rule was actually broken. NORMALIZED-VARIANT AXIS (measured 2026-09-04): avg_stable_rank/d_model is RED, and it fails the same way geometry_schatten's row_normalized_* did. Stable rank is invariant to the ambient width it is divided by: zero-padding a fixed 64x64 operator into d = 64...4096 leaves stable_rank at 15.846333 in every case while stable_rank/d falls 64x. Stable rank tracks d only for iid-Gaussian spectra (measured exponent d^+0.993); for the heavy-tailed spectra trained weights actually have it is nearly d-independent (sigma_i ~ i^-0.5 gives d^+0.157, i^-1.0 gives d^+0.002), and real matrices occupy only 5.0-11.0% of the min(m,n) bound, with occupancy falling as width grows. Across 27 freshly analysed models mean stable rank goes as d^+0.873 and across the 66-model archive as d^+0.736, so dividing by d^1 over-corrects. Consequence on the archive: raw rho +0.793 (d_model) / +0.585 (n_layers) becomes -0.575 (p = 4e-07) / -0.557 (p = 1e-06); on 20 fresh models +0.849 (p = 2e-06) / +0.405 becomes -0.291 / +0.400. Also delete the two dead entries -- geometry_spectral emits only avg_stable_rank, and min_stable_rank / max_stable_rank appear nowhere in src/ nor in any archived result, so those normalizers can never fire.
